supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Folk‑centric acoustic set with strong To Lay Me Down and gospel flair
ai_show_review.blurb: The seven‑song acoustic set showcases Garcia’s crisp picking, a heartfelt vocal on Swing Low (Sweet Chariot), and tight harmonies. Highlights include To Lay Me Down, Rosa Lee McFall and the gospel‑tinged closing number, while a brief New Riders of the Purple Sage segment adds extra color.
ai_show_review.review: On July 30, 1970 at Lion’s Share the Dead delivered a short but reverent acoustic set that feels like a folk‑gospel church service. Jerry Garcia’s fingerpicking is front‑and‑center, his voice carries the soulful swing of “Swing Low (Sweet Chariot)”, and he even drops a quick curse at an over‑eager heckler – evidence of the band’s unfiltered intimacy. Phil Lesh lays down a warm, resonant bass line that anchors the set, though it pushes forward in the mix on some passages. The set closes with “Rosa Lee McFall” and a gospel‑flavored finish, then slips into a fleeting New Riders of the Purple Sage cameo featuring Garcia’s mandolin work and Mickey Hart’s tasteful percussion. While the performance is musically solid, the show’s brevity leaves listeners wanting more, and recording quality varies: the Cotsman soundboard capture is clear but bass‑heavy, whereas an alternate source suffers from generational hiss.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard source that captures the full acoustic set with clear detail, despite a slightly over‑present bass.

key_highlights: Standout acoustic performances of To Lay Me Down, Rosa Lee McFall, and Swing Low (Sweet Chariot).
Garcia’s picking and vocal work shine; brief New Riders of the Purple Sage segment adds variety.
Recording quality: good soundboard capture with a bit too forward bass; alternative source has noticeable hiss.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers crisp acoustic picking, leads the vocal on Swing Low (Sweet Chariot) and even throws a brief curse at a heckler; his playing shines in the NRPS mandolin‑guitar segment.
band_performance.Phil: Phil’s bass is warm and supportive but occasionally sits too forward, making the mix a bit muddy.
band_performance.Mickey: Mickey Hart provides tasteful percussion on the New Riders of the Purple Sage mini‑set.
